title: The Promise of Maple Hollow
premise: Ansel Joubert inherited Maple Hollow Vineyard along with a mountain of debt and a family that treats him as the failure who stayed. When his ex-fiancée's wedding forces him to bring a date, he hires Wren Calloway, a seasonal cellar hand with her own reasons for hiding, and their staged romance turns devastatingly real. As creditors circle and Ansel discovers Wren once worked for the bank foreclosing on him, both must confront the versions of themselves they've been apologizing for. In the end, they save the vineyard not through money but by telling the truth — and choose each other with open eyes.
about_author: Kestrel Kavanagh is the pen name of a former sommelier who spent a decade in small vineyards before turning to writing full-time. They live in a converted farmhouse where they write love stories about people learning to forgive themselves first.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Opening on harvest season at a failing vineyard, Ansel fields another call from creditors while preparing for his sister's reunion-weekend wedding. A letter reveals the bank has assigned a new officer to his file. The beat: weary resignation masking fear, establishing what survival has cost him.

chapters.title: The Cellar Hand Who Doesn't Flinch
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren arrives for seasonal work, competent and guarded, deflecting Ansel's questions about her past with practiced ease. When she overhears him rehearsing excuses for arriving at the wedding alone, she offers — flatly, transactionally — to be his fake girlfriend. The beat: two guarded people recognizing each other's armor.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They negotiate rules over cheap wine: no real names from the past, no kissing unless necessary, walk away clean after dessert. Ansel teaches Wren to prune vines; she catches him lying to his mother by phone. The beat: warmth creeping into a contract neither will admit is working.

chapters.title: Maple Hollow Reunion
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The family estate swallows them whole: his ex-fiancée radiant, his brother condescending, his mother performing pride she doesn't feel. Wren plays her role so well it unsettles him — she knows how families perform because hers shattered. The beat: belonging glimpsed through glass, achingly out of reach.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. During toasts, Ansel defends Wren against a pointed jab about 'hired help,' and something shifts. On the porch afterward, almost-kiss interrupted by a call: the bank moved up his deadline. Wren goes pale — she recognizes the name of the loan officer. The beat: desire colliding with dread; her secret tightening.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Hides
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Back home, Ansel finds Wren's old business card from the bank among her things. Confrontation: she was the analyst who flagged his loan for review years ago — the first domino of his ruin. She insists she tried to stop the foreclosure wave from inside. The beat: betrayal, then the terrible recognition that he's angry at the mirror.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren tells her full story: she approved loans she knew were predatory to keep her own family solvent, and has been paying for it ever since. Ansel, alone in the cellar, admits he let the vineyard decay as self-punishment for surviving when his father didn't. The beat: parallel confessions; forgiveness of others begins with facing oneself.

chapters.title: Running Out of Time
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With forty-eight hours before foreclosure, they audit every ledger together and find evidence the bank falsified Ansel's missed-payment records — paper trail Wren knows how to read. Racing to gather documents, they're caught in a storm and take shelter in the barrel room. First real kiss. The beat: urgency fused with tenderness.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Climax. At the emergency review, Wren testifies to the falsification pattern despite risking her professional reputation entirely. The bank relents pending investigation; the Joubert family, watching, finally sees Ansel clearly — and he sees himself. His brother offers an apology that costs him something. The beat: public vindication, private reckoning.

chapters.title: Second Chances, Better Timing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Resolution. Spring planting: the vineyard survives under a restructured loan, and Wren stays — not hired this time, chosen. At the row where they first pruned together, Ansel asks for a real date, no terms. She says yes before he finishes. The beat: belonging earned, memory honored, survival transformed into a life worth keeping.
